body:
## Summary

Issue #2154 reported three Telegram invocations (`/codex`, `/claude`, `/agent` with `—model formal-ai`) that all died the same way — `docker run … ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:0.339.1` → `Unable to find image … locally` / `unauthorized` — and then reported three *observability* failures on top of it: nothing about the failures appeared in the bot log, no UUID was ever shown for a task's log, and the tasks were absent from `$ --list`.

Ten root causes were found (**RC-A … RC-J**). Seven are code defects and are fixed here, one is upstream, two are documented behaviours. The full analysis, timeline and evidence live in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2154/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2154/README.md).

Fixes #2154

## Root causes

| # | Root cause | Status |
|---|---|---|
| RC-A | `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai` is **private** — anonymous token probe returns `401 UNAUTHORIZED` for the repo and `200` for public peers, so the image exists but is not readable | Reported upstream: link-assistant/formal-ai#1001 |
| RC-B | Hive Mind never authenticates to a registry | Documented (by design) |
| RC-C | The sidecar was launched with an implicit `docker run` pull, so the failure surfaced as a raw argv dump instead of a resolvable error | **Fixed** (`33137125`) |
| RC-D | A launch that never produced a container failed **silently** — no stderr, no structured event | **Fixed** (`4496aa27`) |
| RC-E | The Telegram failure reply dropped the session UUID, leaving nothing to search for | **Fixed** (`4496aa27`) |
| RC-F | Refused sessions stayed tracked, so `/queue` and the monitor disagreed with reality | **Fixed** (`4496aa27`) |
| RC-G | The auto-updater logged the identical `⚠️ Could not pull …: unauthorized` **151 times over 12.5 h** without ever escalating | **Fixed** (`279f8560`) |
| RC-H | The queue recorded a refused launch as `Finished: … (started)` | **Fixed** (`4496aa27`) |
| RC-I | `session_untracked` carried no reason, so the durable log could not explain a disappearance | **Fixed** (`7a46a3ae`) |
| RC-J | **Two UUIDs per task, only one ever shown** — see below | **Fixed** (`97b034f9`) |

### RC-J — why "these tasks are not in list"

Every isolated task carries *two* UUIDs:

| UUID | Minted by | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| **session** | Hive Mind | `--session` argument, container name, Telegram reply, structured log, session snapshot |
| **execution** | start-command | launch banner, `uuid` field of `$ --status`, **and the only identifier `$ --list` prints** |

Hive Mind reported the session UUID everywhere and the execution UUID nowhere. So when the maintainer compared the bot against `$ --list` and saw `d5b8f0af-…` / `edc7b051-…`, nothing the bot had ever printed could be matched against them — including for the two tasks that were running perfectly well. The tasks *were* in the list; they were unrecognisable.

This PR parses the execution UUID from the launch banner (or a JSON launch record), returns it from `executeWithIsolation()`, stores it on the session, persists it, puts it on the `session_tracked` event, shows it next to the session UUID in both the *executing* and *completion* Telegram replies, and **backfills it from `$ --status`** for sessions launched before this fix or whose banner could not be parsed. When it genuinely cannot be determined the code returns `null` rather than guessing — a false correlation would be worse than none.

## How to reproduce the original failure

```bash
# RC-A: the image is private, not missing
curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:link-assistant/formal-ai:pull" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'   # 401
docker run --rm ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:0.339.1 --version                                                # unauthorized
```

Then, in Telegram, `/solve <url> --model formal-ai` — before this PR the bot fell silent, the reply carried no UUID, and `$ --list` showed nothing recognisable.

## Tests

`tests/test-issue-2154-execution-uuid.mjs` — 12 tests, each written to fail against the pre-fix code first:

- the execution UUID is read from the **verbatim launch banner** taken from the incident log;
- the container/session UUID is **not** mistaken for it;
- plain-text and JSON launch records both parse;
- unparseable output yields `null`, never a guess;
- the executing reply shows both UUIDs, and shows no empty label when there is only one;
- the UUID is persisted and appears on `session_tracked`;
- the Telegram launch path records what the runner reports;
- a session with no execution UUID **learns it from `$ --status`** and rewrites its snapshot;
- the completion reply keeps both UUIDs.

Plus the earlier regression tests for RC-C…RC-I committed on this branch.

```
node scripts/run-tests.mjs --suite default
→ All 391 selected test file(s) passed.
npm run lint          → clean
npm run format:check  → All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

## Case study

[`docs/case-studies/issue-2154/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2154/README.md) reconstructs the timeline from the bot log and container logs, enumerates every requirement in the issue (and re-audits the unfinished requirements of #2146, #2119, #2130 and #2059), documents RC-A…RC-J with quoted evidence and line references, and proposes the solution for each. `MANIFEST.md` carries SHA-256 checksums for all 40 collected artefacts (`sha256sum --check` verified).

## Upstream

- link-assistant/formal-ai#1001 — the release workflow leaves `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai` private; includes the reproducible probe, the `docker login` workaround, and the concrete workflow fix.

commits.messageBody:
Adding .gitkeep for PR creation (default mode).
This file will be removed when the task is complete.

Issue: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2154

Every Formal AI task in issue #2154 died the same way: `docker run` was
handed `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:0.339.1` and the implicit pull was
refused, because packages published with GITHUB_TOKEN are private by default
and Hive Mind never authenticates to a registry. The operator saw the raw
argv dump and nothing else.

Image resolution now happens before anything shells out with the reference:

- `src/formal-ai-image.lib.mjs` preflights each candidate (`docker image
  inspect`, then an explicit `docker pull`) and falls back to the local Hive
  Mind image, which bakes `/usr/local/bin/formal-ai` at the same pinned
  version and is already on any host that runs isolated tasks.
- Registry failures are classified (unauthorized / denied / not-found /
  disk-full / network) and reported with the fix for each, instead of echoing
  the daemon.
- `HIVE_MIND_FORMAL_AI_IMAGE` stays an exact pin: no silent substitution.
- The version floor is enforced against the version `/health` reports, so a
  stale fallback image cannot serve an unsupported formal-ai.
- Issue #2146's fail-closed rule is unchanged: with no usable image the task
  is refused, never downgraded to another model.

`src/hive-mind-image.lib.mjs` carries the image references the isolation
runner and the sidecar now share, avoiding an import cycle; the runner
re-exports them so existing callers are untouched.

The new test reproduces the reported failure verbatim against the pre-fix
code (`Unable to find image ... locally`) and passes with the fix.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(formal-ai): resolve the sidecar image before launching it (#2154)

commits.messageBody:
…ue stats

Issue #2154 reported three Formal AI tasks that failed identically and left
no trace: "in logs of telegram bot there nothing about it", "no way to see
UUIDs of each task's log", "these tasks are not in list".

Three defects behind that, each fixed here:

- Silent refusals (RC-D). The sidecar gate, the isolation runner and the
  Telegram command handler all returned `{ success: false }` to their caller
  and wrote nothing to stderr. The only log line the incident produced was
  `Session … untracked (launch failed before it started)`, which never said
  why. Each layer now logs the session UUID, the backend/tool/model and the
  reason.

- The failure reply dropped the UUID (RC-E/RC-F). The error edit replaced the
  "🔄 Starting..." message that carried it (issue #1946), so the operator lost
  the only handle on the attempt. `formatFailedLaunchMessage` keeps the UUID
  and the isolation backend, and states that the session was never launched —
  which is why it has no log and is absent from `--list`.

- A false positive in the queue (RC-H). `SolveQueue.executeItem` called
  `setStarted()` unconditionally, so a refused launch was counted in
  `stats.totalCompleted`, pushed onto `completed` and logged as
  `Finished: […] (started)`. The bot log claimed three sessions had started
  while `$ --list` showed none; a refused launch is now a FAILED item.

Adds tests/test-issue-2154-launch-failure-visibility.mjs (7 tests) and
tests/test-issue-2154-queue-launch-failure.mjs (5 tests, verified to fail
against the pre-fix queue logic), plus a standalone reproduction in
experiments/issue-2154-launch-failure-silence.mjs that prints 0 stderr lines
on the pre-fix tree and one line per refusing layer on the fixed tree.

Refs #2154

commits.messageBody:
…pdater

Issue #2154. The auto-updater logged the same bland warning every ~5
minutes for hours — "Could not pull ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai …
unauthorized" — and never said that the registry was permanently
refusing us. The operator only learned about it when three Telegram
tasks failed to launch.

`updateFormalAiSidecarWhenIdle` now classifies the pull failure with
`classifyDockerRegistryError`: unauthorized/denied/not-found are
configuration faults, so the warning is escalated (🚨), names the
reason and lists the remediation, and the result carries
`classification`, `permanent` and `remediation` for callers. Transient
failures (network, daemon) keep the old ⚠️ tone.

Also collects the evidence for the case study:

- experiments/issue-2154-ghcr-visibility-probe.mjs, a credential-free
  probe of GHCR's anonymous token endpoint that distinguishes public
  (200), private (401) and absent (403) packages
- docs/case-studies/issue-2154/data with the GitHub JSON for #2154,
  #2146, #2130, #2119, #2059 and their pull requests, the gzipped bot
  log from the incident, the registry probe output and the upstream
  formal-ai release workflow

commits.messageBody:
Issue #2154. The durable bot log recorded `session_untracked
{"sessionName":"4750eeff-…"}` one second after `session_tracked`, with
no reason: the explanation ("launch failed before it started") went to
an untimestamped console line, so the incident could not be
reconstructed from the timestamped stream alone.

`untrackSession` now takes an optional `{ reason }` and emits it with
the event, together with the url, command, tool and isolation backend
of the session that never started. The Telegram launch path passes the
launch error, and the durable store's `complete` event and debug line
carry the reason too.

tests/test-issue-2154-structured-log-reason.mjs fails 0/4 against the
previous code and passes 4/4 with it.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(sessions): record why a session was untracked in the structured log

commits.messageBody:
Issue #2154 reported "no way to see UUIDs of each task's log" and "these
tasks are not in list". Both come from the same gap: every isolated task
carries two UUIDs. Hive Mind mints the session UUID and passes it as
`--session` (it also names the container); start-command mints its own
execution UUID, prints it in the launch banner, returns it as `uuid` in
`$ --status`, and it is the only identifier `$ --list` shows. Telegram,
the structured log and the session snapshot only ever reported the
session UUID, so nothing the bot printed could be matched against
`--list` — not even for the two tasks that ran perfectly well.

- parseStartCommandExecutionUuid() reads the UUID from the launch banner
  (box-drawing or plain) or from a JSON launch record, and returns null
  rather than guessing.
- executeWithIsolation() returns it; the Telegram launch path stores it
  on the session, re-tracks, and shows it next to the session UUID.
- session-monitor backfills it from `$ --status` for sessions launched
  before this fix or whose banner could not be parsed, and persists it.
- The completion reply keeps both UUIDs, so a finished task stays
  findable after the thread goes quiet.
- session_tracked events and the durable snapshot carry it too.

Adds tests/test-issue-2154-execution-uuid.mjs (12 tests) and the
docs/case-studies/issue-2154 case study covering RC-A…RC-J.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(sessions): surface start-command's execution UUID end to end

title: fix(sessions): make refused Formal AI launches visible and tasks findable by UUID
